annotationRationale: The main method models expected remaining waits and averages over the first outcome. The alternative sums probabilities of needing successive games; its geometric-series concept remains specific to that method.

review.questionCheck: Independently, conditioning on the first game gives 1+(1/3)(3/2)+(2/3)(3)=7/2, matching choice D and the key. The stem and choices are consistent; no figures or grading conflicts are supplied.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: No shared-bank methods are supplied. Both third-party references use first-game conditioning, retained in the first method. Summing survival probabilities provides a genuinely different accessible second route. No additional route is needed.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed expectation and state-recursion concepts fit the main method, with independence as support. Infinite geometric series appropriately remains specific to the alternative.
review.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is correct; no area repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The capped waits satisfy g_0=0 and g_m=1+(1-p)g_{m-1}. Their monotone, uniformly bounded means establish a finite uncapped expectation, making g=1+(1-p)g legitimate. The two conditional additional waits are 3/2 and 3, and including the first game gives 7/2.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Both cited references supply the conditional-first-game route. The source-informed-original basis is accurate: the candidate adds its own capped-wait justification and reconstructs the explanation without copying third-party prose. Neither reference is presented as official MAA material.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The opening explains why the first outcome is the useful split. The derivation justifies the waiting-time formula, its finiteness, and why the initial game must be added.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: All three direct nodes apply: state recursion constructs and validates the waiting-time equation, cnm_h252 supplies weighted expectations, and cnm_h141 supports the independent-trial model.

methodReviews.mathCheck: For n>=1, the disjoint all-win and all-loss events give P(T>n)=(1/3)^n+(2/3)^n. The contribution-counting argument justifies summing these tails. Handling n=0 separately avoids double counting, and the convergent sums give 1+1/2+2=7/2.
